canonical_name: UMDHMM 1.02 -- Hidden Markov Model toolkit in C: forward, backward, Viterbi and Baum-Welch (Tapas Kanungo, 1998)
lineage: Rabiner's 1989 tutorial algorithms implemented directly in C at the University of Maryland (1998): esthmm TRAINS an HMM from an observation sequence by Baum-Welch (EM), testfor/testvit evaluate and decode, genseq samples. The classic compact reference many later toolkits cite; complements the vault's decode-only viterbi-hmm-xukmin. Preserved from a GitHub mirror of Kanungo's original distribution (the author's page is gone) -- HISTORICAL_ARCHIVE_MIRROR.
version: UMDHMM 1.02 (VERSION file); mirror github.com/palanceli/UMDHMM master (commit in hashes)

license.status: see COPYING in the tree (Kanungo's terms, research use); recorded, not asserted

entry_points: esthmm (Baum-Welch training), testfor (forward), testvit (Viterbi), genseq; hmm.h; sample models t2.hmm/t3.hmm, sequences t2.*.seq

example.command: make; ./esthmm -S 1 -N 3 -M 2 t2.1500.seq  (trains from t2.1500.seq generated by the 3-state t2.hmm)
example.output: a trained A/B/pi; compared against the generating t2.hmm (the ORACLE, up to state relabelling)

upstream_docs: Rabiner, A Tutorial on Hidden Markov Models and Selected Applications in Speech Recognition, Proc IEEE 1989

human_capability_summary.built_to: learn the transition and emission probabilities of a hidden process from its outputs alone, then decode the hidden states
human_capability_summary.pressure: hidden state with no labels; local optima of EM; sequences long enough for probabilities to underflow (scaling)
human_capability_summary.success_means: the trained model reproduces the generating model's parameters (up to relabelling) and its likelihood on held-out data

known_human_problem_solved: unsupervised learning of a hidden Markov process
human_environmental_pressure: hidden state, unlabeled observations, numerical underflow
human_failure_condition: EM converges to a poor local optimum or the likelihood underflows without scaling
behavioral_entry_point: change -S (the random seed / initial model) and compare the trained models; shorten the training sequence to t2.50.seq

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run umdhmm-kanungo-1.02
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: learn the transition and emission probabilities of a hidden process from its outputs alone, then decode the hidden states
